description: Somos un equipo de alumnos de UABC de 5to Semestre de la carrera de Software y Tecnologias Emergentes, es nuestro primer hackaton de la NASA, tenemos muchisimo entusiasmo e interes de aprender nuevas habilidades y retos para nuestra formacion profesional, personal y escolar .
summary: AgroBytes is a decision-support web app for farmers facing a changing climate. The farmer draws their field on a map, picks their current crop and a priority (save water, improve soil, or keep income). The backend pulls 10 years of NASA POWER climate data for that exact point, plus soil data from ISRIC SoilGrids, and a transparent rules engine recommends seasonal crop rotations. Each option comes with a score, the reasons behind it, risks such as frost, heat, drought or heavy rain, an estimated irrigation need (FAO-56 water balance), and an explicit uncertainty level. A "what if?" mode shows how the recommendation changes if next year is hotter or drier. The idea is to turn NASA Earth-observation data, which is usually hard to use, into explainable recommendations a farmer can act on and share with an agronomist, helping them shift their field toward more resilient, water-efficient rotations.
details:
What it does: A user draws a parcel on a satellite map, chooses the current crop and a priority. The API fetches daily NASA POWER data (temperature, precipitation, solar radiation, humidity, soil moisture) for the last 10 years at that point. It also gets soil texture and pH from ISRIC SoilGrids and scores 18 crops against FAO ECOCROP ranges. A rules engine then builds the current rotation plus 3 alternative strategies. For each one it shows a score, reasons, climate risks, estimated water use (FAO-56 Kc and reference evapotranspiration), a rule-based nitrogen and soil-health estimate, and an uncertainty level. Users can compare options, simulate climate shifts ("what if it's 2 °C hotter / 20 % drier?"), see a crop calendar, export a PDF and keep a history that also works offline (PWA).

Why it matters: NASA data is high quality but hard for farmers to use. AgroBytes keeps it explainable: every number can be traced to a source (documented in docs/METODOLOGIA.md and validated against official crop calendars in docs/VALIDACION.md). It does not claim to be ML; it is a transparent agronomic rules engine.

Tools: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet/react-leaflet, Recharts, jsPDF (frontend); Python, FastAPI, Pydantic, SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL + PostGIS (backend); Docker Compose; GitHub Actions CI.

Limitations: Recommendations are estimates based on historical climate, not forecasts, and they do not replace a local agronomist. Next step: validate with farmers in the Mexicali valley.
dataRefs: NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources) API
